note: Every parameter of the flying-fish simulator, with its source. kind = measured (from a fetched source), secondary (quoted second-hand in a fetched source), assumed (no source; the value is a modelling choice and the slider range shows how much it matters), tuned (chosen so a sourced quantity is reproduced; which one is named). Nothing here comes from a bird.

rho_air.note: sea level; same value as physics/analysis.py

fish.label: Darkedged-wing flying fish, Park and Choi 2010 specimen L3

ref_area_m2.source: park-choi-2010 Table 1 model L3: A1 + A2 + A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform), the reference area of its coefficients

span_m.source: park-choi-2010 Table 1 model L3 (full pectoral span S)

CL_at_zero_deg.source: no value in the text (it is in Fig. 5, not read); chosen inside the plausible range; with LD_max it fixes the drag polar

CL_slope_per_deg.source: (CL_max - CL_at_zero_deg) / 35 deg, linear up to the stall at 35 deg; shape assumed

CD_k.source: CD = CD_min + k CL^2 with k fixed by CD(0 deg) = CL(0 deg) / LD_max; quadratic polar shape assumed

stall_alpha_deg.source: park-choi-2010: lift coefficient largest at 30-35 deg

glide_alpha_deg.source: the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface

body_frontal_area_m2.source: no body depth or width in the sources; 0.0007 m^2 is a 30 mm by 30 mm ellipse-sized section for a 203 mm fish

water_drag_coefficient.source: no measured value for a flying fish; frontal-area drag coefficient of a streamlined body

approach_speed_m_s.source: makiguchi-2013 Discussion citing Davenport 1994: approach and leap at approximately 10 m/s (20 to 30 body lengths per second)

swim_thrust_N.source: set equal to the water drag at the approach speed, so the submerged fish reaches 10 m/s (the secondary field value) and no faster

taxi_thrust_N.source: set to the swim thrust times a factor (default 1); the lower caudal lobe sculls at up to 50 beats per second (davenport-1994) but no thrust was measured; the factor is the slider; validation target: taxi length about 9 m (deng-2019 citing its ref 11) and take-off at about 10 m/s

lobe_length_m.source: length of the enlarged lower caudal lobe below the body axis; not in the sources; 0.05 m is a quarter of standard length

pitch_at_leap_deg.source: makiguchi-2013 Table 3: 20.0 +- 3.3 deg in captivity; field studies cited there give about 30 deg

start_depth_m.source: where the run starts; it only sets how long the swim phase lasts

reentry_min_speed_m_s.source: below this speed at re-entry the fish is taken to stop taxiing and submerge; not in the sources

max_glides.source: stops the run; field sequences of 400 m in 30 s (park-choi-2010 introduction) imply several taxi-glide cycles

ground_effect.source: park-choi-2010 Fig. 12 and text (physics/ground-effect.json): lift unchanged; drag times 1 for h/b >= 0.97, falling linearly to 0.86 at h/b = 0.33 over water, held at 0.86 below that (not measured lower)

taxi_pitch_deg.source: body pitch while taxiing with the tail in the water; not measured. Added after run 1 (recorded as a deviation in physics/sim/RUNS.md): with the body held at the 20 deg leap pitch the fish lifts off at about 10.7 m/s before the tail can accelerate it, so the taxi cannot reach the 15-20 m/s field airspeed. Davenport 1994 says the fish accelerates to take-off speed by taxiing with the tail beating.

validation_targets.source: makiguchi-2013 introduction citing Edgerton and Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990
park-choi-2010 introduction citing Hertel 1966, Rayner 1986, Vogel 1994

validation_targets.quantity: minimum lift-supported speed (constraint C9 in the Lean ledger)
validation_targets.source: physics/results.json interpretation_B from the measured W, S, CL_max
